### `xml.namespace_matches`

tests if XML namespace declarations match expected namespaces

**Use for:** checking which XML dialect/schema version a file uses. Only the root element's own namespace is detected, under prefix ``''``: ElementTree drops ``xmlns:*`` attributes, so other declared prefixes are never seen and expecting them fails.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| expected_namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Required map prefix -> URI, e.g. ``{'': 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'}``; ``None`` is an execution error. |
| check_mode | `str` | `'contains'` | ``contains`` (default; every expected prefix present with that URI) or ``exact`` (dicts equal). Other values are an execution error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_namespace_matches
  function: xml.namespace_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
```

### `xml.values_compare`

compares two values (element text or attribute) of one XML file (or of two files) as numbers or timestamps (earlier/later, within a tolerance, A = B + offset)

**Use for:** relations inside one XML file (or between two, ``other_dst``): a last-saved value later than the first-opened one (two attributes, or two elements), two timestamps within a few seconds of each other, a counter one above another (``comparison_type: equals`` with ``offset: 1``). To compare one value with a constant use xml.element_text_matches or xml.attribute_matches with ``comparison_type``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | Selects the element of the first value (ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset as in xml.element_text_matches). It must select exactly one element (with ``attribute``: one element that has the attribute): nothing fails, several are an error. |
| **other_xpath** | `str` |  | Selects the element of the second value; same rules (may equal ``xpath`` to compare two attributes of one element). |
| attribute | `str \| None` | `None` | Take the first value from this attribute (``{uri}name`` for namespaced attributes); ``None`` (default) takes the element text (``element.text``, before the first child, not stripped). |
| other_attribute | `str \| None` | `None` | The same for the second value. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | How the first value relates to the second: ``equals`` (default), ``not_equals``, ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal`` (``less`` = earlier for timestamps). Other values are an error. |
| value_type | `str` | `'auto'` | ``auto`` (default; numbers if both are numbers, else timestamps), ``number`` or ``timestamp``. A value that is no number or timestamp is an error. |
| tolerance | `int \| float \| None` | `None` | Allowed difference for ``equals``/``not_equals`` (seconds for timestamps). |
| offset | `int \| float \| None` | `None` | Added to the second value before comparing (seconds for timestamps, may be negative; ``'{{ name }}'`` = a saved number): ``first <comparison_type> second + offset``. |
| time_format | `str \| None` | `None` | ``strptime`` format of text timestamps on both sides; default ISO 8601 or RFC 2822. |
| timestamp_epoch | `int \| None` | `None` | Read numbers as a count since 1 January of ``1970``, ``1601`` or ``2001``. |
| timestamp_unit | `str \| None` | `None` | Unit of that count: ``s`` (default), ``ms``, ``us``, ``ns`` or ``100ns``. |
| utc_offset | `str \| None` | `None` | Zone of timestamps without one (``+02:00``); default UTC. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in both XPaths (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |
| other_dst | `str \| None` | `None` | Guest path of a second XML file to read ``other_xpath`` from (same rules as ``dst``, ``archive!/member`` included); default ``None``: ``dst``. A missing file is an error. Compares a file with a copy saved before an action. |
| value_decode | `list[str] \| str \| None` | `None` | Decode both values before comparing (steps as in xml.element_text_matches). |
| decoded_key_path | `str \| None` | `None` | With ``json`` in ``value_decode``: key path into the decoded value; it must select one value: none fails, several are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_values_compare
  function: xml.values_compare
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    other_xpath: <str>
```

### `xml.xpath_result_matches`

tests if XPath expression result matches expected value (text, number, or boolean)

**Use for:** typed checks on the first matched element. Prefer xml.element_text_matches for text.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the XML file; a glob must match exactly one path. A missing file or malformed XML is an execution error. |
| **xpath** | `str` |  | ElementTree ``ElementPath`` subset, evaluated on the root element: ``//tag`` (any depth), ``/root/child`` (first step must be the root tag), ``child/grandchild``, predicates ``[@attr='v']``, ``[tag='v']``, ``[@attr]``. Any ``(``, ``::``, ``..`` or ``\|`` (even inside a quoted value) is an execution error, so no functions such as ``text()``. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool` |  | Required. Converted per ``result_type``: ``str()``, ``float()`` or ``bool()``. Note ``bool('false')`` is True -- use unquoted YAML ``true``/``false``. |
| result_type | `str` | `'text'` | ``text`` (default; first element's ``.text``, ``''`` if none), ``number`` (``float`` of that text; no match -> 0.0, non-numeric -> execution error) or ``boolean`` (whether anything matched). Other values are an execution error. |
| namespaces | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Prefix -> URI map for prefixed names in ``xpath`` (``{ns: 'http://...'}`` + ``//ns:item``); ``{uri}tag`` also works without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_xpath_result_matches
  function: xml.xpath_result_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    xpath: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool>
```

## yaml

### `yaml.contains_key`

tests if a YAML file contains the specified key path (supports several documents)

**Use for:** checking that a settings/config file gained a key. To also check the value use yaml.value_matches; to check that a key is absent use yaml.value_count with ``expected_count: 0`` (or ``expect_to_fail: true`` here: a missing file stays an error).

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file (read with ``safe_load``; UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a BOM). A glob must match exactly one path; ``archive.zip!/member.yaml`` reads an archive member. A missing, unreadable or invalid file is an error. A file with several documents (``---``) is a top-level list, one per document; an empty file has no keys. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root, e.g. ``display.font.size``. ``*`` expands all values of a mapping, ``name[*]`` all elements of sequence ``name``, ``name[0]`` / ``name[-1]`` one element; a leading ``[0]`` / ``[*]`` addresses a top-level sequence or a document of a multi-document file (``[1].kind``, ``[*].kind``). Keys with dots use quotes in brackets (``['app.window'].width``). |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_contains_key
  function: yaml.contains_key
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
```

### `yaml.value_count`

tests how many YAML values exist at a key path, optionally only those matching a value (0 = absent)

**Use for:** counting entries (``recent[*]``, documents ``[*]``) and asserting absence: ``expected_count: 0`` passes when the key path selects nothing (or nothing matches ``expected_value``), while a missing or invalid file is still an error. A path that selects one sequence counts its elements when ``expected_value`` is given; without it every selected value counts once.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file; a glob must match exactly one path. Several documents form a top-level list; an empty file has no values. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root (syntax as in yaml.contains_key). |
| **expected_count** | `int` |  | Non-negative integer to compare with. |
| expected_value | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | Only count values equal to this (normalised as in yaml.value_matches). ``None`` (default) counts every value. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched in ``str(value)``. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``. Other values are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_count
  function: yaml.value_count
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_count: <int>
```

### `yaml.value_matches`

tests if the YAML value at a key path matches the expected value (supports wildcards with any/all modes)

**Use for:** asserting a setting/field value. If the path yields several values (a wildcard, or a sequence value, whose elements are then compared one by one) ``wildcard_mode`` decides. Values keep their YAML 1.1 types (``5`` is an int, ``true``/``yes``/``on`` and ``false``/``no``/``off`` are booleans); dates and timestamps become ISO 8601 strings (``2024-01-15``, ``2024-01-15T10:30:00``, ``+00:00`` for a ``Z`` zone), ``!!binary`` a lowercase hex string.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dst** | `str` |  | Guest path to the YAML file; a glob must match exactly one path. Several documents form a top-level list. A missing or invalid file is an error; an unresolvable key path fails. |
| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path from the root (syntax as in yaml.contains_key), e.g. ``servers[*].port`` or ``[0].kind`` for the first document. |
| **expected_value** | `str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` |  | Compared with Python ``==``, which is type-sensitive (``5`` != ``"5"``; ``null`` needs ``null``). A ``!re`` tag (``re.match``) or ``{{placeholder}}`` compares ``str(value)``. |
| regex_match | `bool` | `False` | Treat a string ``expected_value`` as a regex searched (``re.search``, unanchored) in ``str(value)``. An invalid regex is an error. |
| wildcard_mode | `str` | `'any'` | ``any`` (default): one value must match; ``all``: every value must match. Other values are an error. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | ``equals`` (default), ``not_equals``, ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal``. Anything but ``equals``, or any parameter below, compares the value with ``expected_value`` as a number or point in time (ordered mode; ``less`` = earlier); ``!re`` / ``regex_match`` are then errors, a lone ``{{ name }}`` is the saved variable; a value that is no number or timestamp is an error. |
| value_type | `str` | `'auto'` | ``auto`` (default; numbers if both sides are numbers, else timestamps), ``number`` or ``timestamp``. |
| tolerance | `int \| float \| None` | `None` | Allowed difference for ``equals``/``not_equals`` (seconds for timestamps). |
| time_format | `str \| None` | `None` | ``strptime`` format of text timestamps on both sides; default ISO 8601 or RFC 2822. |
| timestamp_epoch | `int \| None` | `None` | Read numbers as a count since 1 January of ``1970``, ``1601`` or ``2001``. |
| timestamp_unit | `str \| None` | `None` | Unit of that count: ``s`` (default), ``ms``, ``us``, ``ns`` or ``100ns``. |
| utc_offset | `str \| None` | `None` | Zone of timestamps without one (``+02:00``); default UTC. |
| value_decode | `list[str] \| str \| None` | `None` | Decode the value read from the file before comparing: one step or a list applied in order: ``url`` (percent-decoding), ``base64``, ``hex``, ``utf16`` (bytes as UTF-16 text), ``json`` (parse, then take ``decoded_key_path``). Bytes left at the end are UTF-8 text, else hex. A value a step cannot decode, or an unknown step, is an error. |
| decoded_key_path | `str \| None` | `None` | Key path into the value ``json`` decoded (syntax as in ``key_path``); it must select one value: none fails (the value decoded, the key is not in it), several are an error. Required with ``json``, an error without it. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_value_matches
  function: yaml.value_matches
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    expected_value: <str | int | float | bool | None>
```

### `yaml.values_compare`

compares two values of one YAML file (or of two files) as numbers or timestamps (earlier/later, within a tolerance, A = B + offset)

**Use for:** relations inside one file (or between two, ``other_dst``): a last-saved value later than the first-opened one, two timestamps within a few seconds of each other, a counter one above another (``comparison_type: equals`` with ``offset: 1``). To compare one value with a constant use yaml.value_matches with ``comparison_type``.

*FILE_CONTENT*, os: any

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|

| **key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path of the first value (syntax as in yaml.contains_key). It must select exactly one value (a one-element array counts as its element): nothing fails, several values are an error. |
| **other_key_path** | `str` |  | Dot path of the second value; same rules. |
| comparison_type | `str` | `'equals'` | How the first value relates to the second: ``equals`` (default), ``not_equals``, ``greater``, ``less``, ``greater_equal`` or ``less_equal`` (``less`` = earlier for timestamps). Other values are an error. |
| value_type | `str` | `'auto'` | ``auto`` (default; numbers if both are numbers, else timestamps), ``number`` or ``timestamp``. A value that is no number or timestamp is an error. |
| tolerance | `int \| float \| None` | `None` | Allowed difference for ``equals``/``not_equals`` (seconds for timestamps). |
| offset | `int \| float \| None` | `None` | Added to the second value before comparing (seconds for timestamps, may be negative; ``'{{ name }}'`` = a saved number): ``first <comparison_type> second + offset``. |
| time_format | `str \| None` | `None` | ``strptime`` format of text timestamps on both sides; default ISO 8601 or RFC 2822. |
| timestamp_epoch | `int \| None` | `None` | Read numbers as a count since 1 January of ``1970``, ``1601`` or ``2001``. |
| timestamp_unit | `str \| None` | `None` | Unit of that count: ``s`` (default), ``ms``, ``us``, ``ns`` or ``100ns``. |
| utc_offset | `str \| None` | `None` | Zone of timestamps without one (``+02:00``); default UTC. |
| other_dst | `str \| None` | `None` | Guest path of a second file to read ``other_key_path`` from (same rules as ``dst``, ``archive!/member`` included); default ``None``: ``dst``. A missing file is an error. Compares a file with a copy saved before an action. |
| value_decode | `list[str] \| str \| None` | `None` | Decode both values before comparing (steps as in yaml.value_matches). |
| decoded_key_path | `str \| None` | `None` | With ``json`` in ``value_decode``: key path into the decoded value; it must select one value: none fails, several are an error. |

```yaml
tests:
- name: check_values_compare
  function: yaml.values_compare
  parameter:
    dst: <str>
    key_path: <str>
    other_key_path: <str>
```
